search.query: ((("temporal lobe epilep*"[tiab] OR TLE[tiab] OR "mesial temporal sclerosis"[tiab] OR "hippocampal sclerosis"[tiab] OR "medial temporal lobe epilep*"[tiab]) AND ("voxel-based morphometr*"[tiab] OR VBM[tiab] OR "gray matter"[tiab] OR "grey matter"[tiab] OR "cortical thickness"[tiab] OR "structural MRI"[tiab] OR "hippocampal volum*"[tiab] OR morphometr*[tiab] OR atrophy[tiab])) AND ("magnetic resonance imaging"[Mesh] OR MRI[tiab]) AND "Humans"[MeSH])

abstract.objective: Meta-analysis of structural neuroimaging studies reporting grey-matter or volumetric differences between temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) patients and healthy controls, where the side of the seizure focus is specified.
inclusion_criteria: Empirical English-language structural MRI studies (VBM, cortical thickness, or volumetry) comparing TLE patients against a control group.

The study must report, or make determinable, the side of the seizure focus (left, right, or both/mixed). Studies of unspecified laterality still qualify at abstract stage; laterality is resolved at full text.
Mesial temporal sclerosis, hippocampal sclerosis and medial temporal lobe epilepsy all qualify as TLE.
exclusion_criteria: Reviews, meta-analyses, case reports, and studies of a single patient.
Purely functional studies (fMRI, PET, MEG, EEG) with no structural morphometric outcome.
Studies only of post-surgical change with no patient-versus-control comparison.

inclusion.I1: Empirical English-language structural MRI studies (VBM, cortical thickness, or volumetry) comparing TLE patients against a control group.
inclusion.I2: The study must report, or make determinable, the side of the seizure focus (left, right, or both/mixed). Studies of unspecified laterality still qualify at abstract stage; laterality is resolved at full text.
inclusion.I3: Mesial temporal sclerosis, hippocampal sclerosis and medial temporal lobe epilepsy all qualify as TLE.

exclusion.E1: Reviews, meta-analyses, case reports, and studies of a single patient.
exclusion.E2: Purely functional studies (fMRI, PET, MEG, EEG) with no structural morphometric outcome.
exclusion.E3: Studies only of post-surgical change with no patient-versus-control comparison.

fulltext.objective: Confirm the study reports stereotactic coordinates for a structural comparison between TLE patients and controls, with the seizure-focus side determinable.
inclusion_criteria: Reports coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) for at least one patient-versus-control structural contrast.
The seizure-focus side of the patient sample is stated or clearly determinable.
Whole-brain or whole-region analysis; ROI-only hippocampal volumetry without coordinates does NOT qualify.
exclusion_criteria: Coordinates reported only for functional or diffusion measures, not grey matter structure.
Patient group is not TLE, or is a mixed epilepsy sample where TLE cannot be isolated.

inclusion.I4: Reports coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) for at least one patient-versus-control structural contrast.
inclusion.I5: The seizure-focus side of the patient sample is stated or clearly determinable.
inclusion.I6: Whole-brain or whole-region analysis; ROI-only hippocampal volumetry without coordinates does NOT qualify.

exclusion.E6: Coordinates reported only for functional or diffusion measures, not grey matter structure.
exclusion.E7: Patient group is not TLE, or is a mixed epilepsy sample where TLE cannot be isolated.

inclusion_criteria: Judge each analysis from its own name, description and table caption, plus the study text for the seizure-focus side. An empty or generic analysis name is never itself a reason to exclude.
Coordinates must be in MNI or Talairach space.
exclusion_criteria: Exclude analyses that are not a patient-versus-control structural comparison.

annotations.name: left_tle_atrophy
inclusion_criteria: The patient sample has a LEFT-sided seizure focus (left TLE, left MTS, left hippocampal sclerosis). If the paper reports left and right groups separately, this label applies only to the left-focus contrast.
The contrast direction is controls GREATER than patients, i.e. atrophy / reduced grey matter / reduced volume in patients.
exclusion_criteria: Patients GREATER than controls (hypertrophy or increased volume).
Contrasts between two patient groups rather than patients versus controls.

annotations.name: right_tle_atrophy
inclusion_criteria: The patient sample has a RIGHT-sided seizure focus (right TLE, right MTS, right hippocampal sclerosis). If left and right groups are reported separately, this label applies only to the right-focus contrast.
The contrast direction is controls GREATER than patients.
exclusion_criteria: Contrasts between two patient groups rather than patients versus controls.

annotations.name: all_tle_atrophy
inclusion_criteria: Any TLE patient sample (left, right, bilateral or unspecified) versus controls.
The contrast direction is controls GREATER than patients.
exclusion_criteria: Contrasts between two patient groups rather than patients versus controls.

studies.title: The role of the amygdala in ictal central apnea: insights from brain MRI morphometry.
studies.abstract: Ictal central apnea (ICA) is a frequent correlate of focal seizures, particularly in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), and regarded as a potential electroclinical biomarker of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP). Aims of this study are to investigate morphometric changes of subcortical structures in ICA patients and to find neuroimaging biomarkers of ICA in patients with focal epilepsy.
studies.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
studies.abstract_screening_reason: Study uses structural MRI morphometry in focal epilepsy/ICA and references TLE, but the abstract does not clearly state a patient-versus-healthy-control comparison or specify seizure-focus laterality. Insufficient information to confirm I1 and I2/I3 from the abstract alone; include for full-text review to determine eligibility.
studies.fulltext_screening_reason: The full text reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space from voxel-based morphometry (e.g., MNI X: −21, Y: −3, Z: −18; T=4.21) for patient-versus-control structural contrasts (VBM whole-brain analyses and a TLE sub-analysis). The seizure-focus side is stated and determinable: the methods describe flipping images to place the epileptic hemisphere on the left and report results ipsilateral/contralateral to the epileptogenic zone (EZ). The structural analysis is whole-brain VBM (not ROI-only hippocampal volumetry). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

studies.title: Clinical significance of serological biomarkers and neuropsychological performances in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy.
studies.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a common form of focal epilepsy. Serum biomarkers to predict cognitive performance in TLE patients without psychiatric comorbidities and the link with gray matter (GM) atrophy have not been fully explored.
studies.abstract_screening_reason: Abstract discusses gray-matter atrophy in TLE but does not specify whether structural MRI measures were compared against healthy controls or report seizure laterality. Insufficient information to confirm I1 or laterality, so include for full-text review.
studies.fulltext_screening_reason: The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) results with stereotactic coordinates in Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space (e.g., [x,y,z] coordinates in tables/figures) for patient-versus-control gray matter contrasts. The patient sample is clearly temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) and the seizure-focus side is provided (21 left, 13 right), so focus laterality is determinable. The analysis used whole-brain VBM (not hippocampal-only ROI volumetry). The article includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

activation_tables.table_foot: [x,y,z] refers to Montreal Neurological Institute coordinates. T values were determined by dividing the estimated regression coefficient by its standard error
